is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses exclusively on Culex quinquefasciatus (Title, Abstract, Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper genotypes the kdr-like mutation L982F, which it identifies as the canonical L1014F mutation (Abstract, Page 1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) and frequencies are provided for six operational areas in Table 2 and Figure 8.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from Harris County, Texas, USA (Title, Abstract, Page 1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting new field collections, bioassays, and genotyping data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is reported for six specific operational areas (sites) within Harris County, Texas (Page 4, Fig 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito egg rafts were collected in the field in 2018 (Page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study reports routine new field collections and bioassays conducted by local mosquito control and university researchers in Texas.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype and bioassay data are contained within the main text, tables, and figures.

assessment.summary: The study investigates the frequency of the kdr-like mutation (L982F, equivalent to L1014F) in Culex quinquefasciatus populations from six areas in Harris County, Texas, and evaluates its impact on survivorship following field-cage permethrin tests.
exclusion_reasons: Not an African field population (study conducted in Texas, USA)
